content.text: Let me construct properly: 8 modules of "GGGGGGGGGUUUUCCCCCCCCC" (22 nt) joined by "A" = 22×8 + 7 = 183.

The issue: hairpin modules stack together across the linker when all-GC. I need to break cross-module pairing. The target has each helix as 9bp with 4-nt loop. Within a 22-nt module the helix is self-contained. But consecutive modules form long-range pseudoknots. Let me add strong internal closing and reduce cross-module complementarity. Use "A" linker was right but adjacent helices still pair across (positions 0-159, etc.). I need to break the inter-module stacking by alternating.

Let me check current fold and try varying linkers and loop sequences.
The 7 modules collapse into one giant nested helix (long-range pairing across modules). Solution: alternate G-C modules with A-U modules so adjacent arms aren't complementary.

    s=s+'A'+m
print(len(s))
print(s)

content.text:
Still bad - A-U modules aren't forming their hairpins (they pair across to other modules). The core problem: 8 identical modules are intrinsically multivalent. I need each module to be unique so it can only fold onto itself.

Let me use RNA inverse folding via ViennaRNA directly to solve this properly.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/solve.py << 'EOF'
import subprocess, sys
try:
    import RNA
except ImportError:
    print("no RNA module", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)

target = "(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....))))))))).(((((((((....)))))))))"

# Try inverse_fold
seq, dist = RNA.inverse_fold("G"*183, target)
print("dist", dist)
print("seq", seq)
print("len", len(seq))
EOF
python3 /tmp/solve.py
